items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Gene Krupa had his trio then, and it featured Charlie Ventura on tenor saxophone and a pianist, Marty Napoleon.

ctx.x: No, it wasn't Oscar Pettiford. I don't remember who the bass player was. Then on another one, they had Gene Krupa. Gene Krupa had his trio then, and it featured Charlie Ventura on tenor saxophone and a pianist, Marty Napoleon. We would do these things every Monday, and they would record them or make transcriptions or something, and send them overseas for the soldiers as entertainment. Because there was no such thing as television during those days. Either they had live shows that went over, like shows that Bob…

I guess from the way our shows went, I'd imagine most of them were geared toward the Black soldiers or sailors or whatever. Anyway, later on, these transcriptions turned up, and now they can be bought as recordings. I think they were first found in Japan, and then later someone in England had them. But just what label they were under, I have no idea.
